extracted.intended_audience: applicants for and holders of international registrations of marks; officials of competent trademark administrations (Members of the Madrid Union)
extracted.subtask_description: Comprehensive procedural and substantive guidance for preparing, filing, prosecuting and managing international trademark applications and registrations under the Madrid Protocol and its Regulations. Covers form items, fees, time limits, communications, refusals, post-registration recordings (changes, limitation, cancellation, division, replacement, seniority), and use of WIPO online tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may use the Madrid System (Eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets out which natural and legal persons are entitled to file an international application under the Protocol (i.e. entitlement/entitlement to file; basic application or basic registration; Office of origin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains entitlement requirements (nationality, domicile, real and effective industrial or commercial establishment) and related evidence; covers several applicants and how entitlement is shown on the international application (see Item 3). Advises applicants to check Office-of-origin rules and to ensure the basic application/registration exists and supports the international filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive requirements of the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists the mandatory elements of the international application (basic registration/application reference, applicant name and address, appointment of representative if any, indication of goods and services, mark representation and indications, designations, priority claims, signatures and certification by Office of origin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the content of the application form and each item (Items 1–13): how to fill name/address/e-mail/correspondence address; rules for several applicants; preferred language for correspondence; Item 5 (basic application/registration) requirements; Item 6 (priority) and supporting documents; Item 7 (the mark) including special kinds of marks, color claims and standard character marks; Item 9 miscellaneous indications (transliteration, translation, disclaimers, verbal elements, descriptions); Item 10 goods and services (classification, indications); Item 11 designations; Item 12 applicant signature; Item 13 certification and signature by the Office of origin. Includes fee calculation sheet guidance (how fees are computed on filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Mark: representation, color and special kinds
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for the representation of the mark in the international application, including special types (figurative, sound, position, hologram etc.), claims to color, and use of standard characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when a mark must be represented graphically, how to indicate color(s) claimed, when to submit reproductions or descriptions for non-visual marks, and how verbal elements and disclaimers should be indicated. Provides examples and notes on equivalence and transcription for multilingual filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goods and services: indication, classification and irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing how goods and services must be indicated in the international application, including correct classification and level of detail; identifies irregularities in classification or indication of goods/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes acceptable wording, use of the Madrid Goods and Services Manager, when the Office of origin or applicant must remedy irregularities, and consequences of vague or overly broad descriptions. Provides procedures for remedial statements and the allocation of responsibility for corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designations and subsequent designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and substantive rules for designating Contracting Parties in the international application and for presenting subsequent designations after registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies entitlement to make subsequent designations, official forms and required items (MM2 etc.), language of subsequent designation, how to indicate goods/services for the designation, interaction with seniority claims and declarations (EU specifics), and recording/publication of subsequent designations and their effects (date of subsequent designation; periods of protection; possible refusals by designated Offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of protection: grounds, time limits and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets out the grounds on which a designated Contracting Party may refuse protection and the time limits and procedure that apply to notifications of refusal or provisional refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details typical grounds (e.g. absolute/relative grounds under national law), statutory time limits for notifying provisional and final refusals to the International Bureau, required contents of the notification (including additional contents where provisional refusal is based on opposition), language requirements for notifications, recording/publication of refusals, and follow-up procedures (holder responses, appeals, further decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications from Offices via the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: How Offices of designated Contracting Parties and the International Bureau communicate official positions, notifications, decisions and irregularities in the international procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains transmission channels (International Bureau), content and format of communications, how notifications are recorded and published in the Gazette and International Register, and the obligations of Offices to notify decisions (e.g. on provisional refusals, seniority, replacement-taking-notes). Includes treatment of irregular notifications and correction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and calculation of time limits (including continued processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for calculating statutory time limits under the Protocol and Regulations and relief mechanisms where time limits are missed (e.g. continued processing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how time limits are computed, effects of electronic vs postal transmissions, irregularities in postal/delivery services or electronic communications, special COVID-19 considerations, the remedy of continued processing (MM20), applicable fees for continued processing, and the narrow windows and documentary compliance required for relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees: currency, mode, dates, and fee reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for payment of filing, renewal and recording fees to the International Bureau, including acceptable currencies, payment methods, dates of payment and fee reduction provisions for applicants from Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies modes of payment (debit from WIPO account, other methods), how fees are calculated and shown on the fee calculation sheet, what constitutes the date of payment, procedures for changes in fee amounts, and eligibility and procedures to obtain the LDC fee reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on appointment, scope and form of representatives acting before the International Bureau in international applications, subsequent designations and other requests (including cancellation of appointment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers methods of appointment (in application/subsequent designation or separate communication), requirement that only one representative be recorded, how to record and notify appointments or cancellations, legal effect of appointment, irregular appointments, and that recording of appointment carries no fee. Also explains signature requirements when a representative is appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregularities in the international application and how they are remedied
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of irregularities (classification, goods/services indication, formal defects) and who must remedy them (Office of origin or applicant), and the procedural consequences of unresolved irregularities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies irregularities remediable by Office of origin, irregularities to be remedied by applicant, and those that may be remedied by either. Provides timelines for remedial actions, effects on registration dates, and examples of common irregularities (missing certification, incorrect classification, inadequate mark representation) and how to correct them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording, publication and contents of the International Register and Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: What information is recorded in the International Register and published in the WIPO Gazette of International Marks, and the legal effects of such recording and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes contents (holder, mark, goods/services, designations, priority, dates, recorded changes such as limitation/renunciation/cancellation, replacement notifications and seniority claims), the language(s) of publication/registration, legalization of extracts, and how published information creates public notice to third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes and other recordings (change of name/address, legal nature, representative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures, required forms (e.g. MM9), and substantive checks for requests to record changes to holder or representative information in the International Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the items required on the forms (international reg. number, name/address, legal nature), the effect of the recording, fees and fee calculation sheets where applicable, irregular request handling, and publication/notification practices following recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation, renunciation and cancellation of international registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and required forms for limiting the list of goods/services, renouncing protection in designated Contracting Parties, and requesting cancellation of the international registration (or parts thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies form content, required signatures, how limitation affects scope and national/regional co-existing rights, fees (limitation fee calculation), consequences (recording, notification, publication), and procedures where a declaration that a limitation has no effect is filed by an Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in ownership (assignment) of international registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Entitlement of transferee to be recorded as the new holder, required documentary evidence and the official form and items to request a recording of change of ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details evidentiary requirements to demonstrate transfer (local laws/registration), effect of recording on rights, scope (partial or full assignments), fee and irregular request procedures, signature requirements of transferor and/or transferee, and publication/notification practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of an international registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure, forms and effects for dividing an international registration into two or more registrations (including items required for MM-form for division).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the required form items (office presenting request, international registration number, goods/services to be divided, signature), payment information, grounds and legal effects of division, handling of irregular requests, recording in the International Register and notification to the holder and third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of earlier national or regional registration by an international registration (Article 4bis/Rule 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions and effects under Article 4bis and Rule 21 whereby a national or regional registration may be replaced (totally or partially) by an international registration; and procedure for an Office to take note in its register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that replacement can be total or partial (overlap between lists required — at least some goods/services must be equivalent and overlapping), that replacement does not automatically cancel the national/regional registration (co-existence is possible), that holders may request an Office to take note (using local procedures/forms and fees), Office notification to the International Bureau (elements to include: international reg. number, filing/registration numbers and dates, priority date, and if partial, the goods/services concerned), recording/publication by the International Bureau (Model Form MF17), transitional provisions for Rule 21 amendment, and strategic considerations (portfolio centralization benefits versus keeping national registrations during five-year dependency period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seniority claims (recording and notifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: How seniority claims are handled where an international registration is recorded for a designation (notably EU designation), including when EUIPO examines and notifies the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that a seniority claim recorded in the International Register is examined by the designated Office (e.g., EUIPO) which may accept or refuse; where accepted (and recorded) the Office must notify the International Bureau with required particulars (international reg. number; member State(s) and registration numbers/dates). Where later final decisions affect seniority (withdrawal/cancellation), those must be notified. Also explains special treatment of 'late' seniority claims under EU procedures and when notifications to the International Bureau are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation of effects in successor States
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure where a predecessor Contracting Party's territory becomes a successor State and holders may request continuation of effects of an international registration in the successor State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that successors may deposit declaration of continuation (Rule 39); holders notified by IB must file a request within six months and pay a specified fee to maintain protection in the successor State; if missed, continued processing (MM20) may be requested within two months with compliance and fee; after those periods protection can only be obtained by subsequent designation; Offices of successor States may have limited grounds to refuse (e.g. if Article 5(2) time limit had not expired). Recording and publication steps by the IB follow receipt of request and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications: methods, official forms, signatures, languages and trilingual regime
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted methods of communication with the International Bureau (written, electronic), official forms (MM-series), signature requirements, optional continuation sheets and the multilingual/trilingual regime for processing and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides rules on which communications must be in writing, which are handled electronically, how to indicate dates, use of continuation sheets, when and how signatures must be supplied, consequences of irregular or unsigned communications, and the interplay of English/French/Spanish (trilingual regime) for filings, notifications and publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online services, public information and tools (Madrid Monitor, Madrid Goods and Services Manager, Application Assistant, Portfolio Manager)
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and role of WIPO's online tools and public databases to assist filing, searching and management of international registrations and to provide public access to application/registration data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the services (Madrid Monitor, Goods and Services Manager, Application Assistant, Member Profiles Database, Madrid Portfolio Manager, online renewal and subsequent designation, online payment and forms), explains their intended use (assistance with correct classification, drafting indications, monitoring status, filing electronically), and notes extract/legalization procedures, statistics, and publication of extracts.
